children: UK diamond producer's H1 revenue rose 32% yr/yr, driven by higher prices and quality
Company returned to profit in H1 with EPS of 0.5 US cents, after prior-year loss
Cost control and royalty relief supported improved EBITDA and reduced net debt
Gem Diamonds says FY2026 production and cost forecasts remain in line with guidance
Company says diamond market recovery timing and extent remain uncertain
Gem Diamonds is in talks to renew or extend revolving credit facilities expiring December 2026
HIGHER PRICES AND QUALITY - Co said increased revenue was due to improved quality of diamonds sold and higher prices achieved
COST REDUCTIONS - Structural cost measures and the Business Resilience Programme implemented in July 2025 materially reduced operating costs, per CEO Clifford Elphick
ROYALTY RELIEF - Extended suspension of Letšeng royalties lowered selling costs and supported profitability
The one available analyst rating on the shares is "strong buy"
The average consensus recommendation for the non-gold precious metals & minerals peer group is "buy."
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Gem Diamonds Ltd is GBp13.00, about 108% above its September 2 closing price of GBp6.25
